name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 2026 European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) will be held in Vienna, Austria from 6 to 10 July and targets PhD students and young researchers working in all aspects of AI. It offers a one‑week intensive program with introductory and advanced courses, specialized tutorials on Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, and a rich social programme including a reception at the Vienna City Hall. The school is co‑located with the 5th ACM Europe Digital Humanism Summer School and features over 30 lecturers across six parallel tracks.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
venue: Skeikampen Conference Hotel, near Oslo, Norway
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is organized by the Nordic Language Processing Laboratory and the University of Oslo in Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC consortium countries, and offers technical presentations, hands‑on elements, and discussions on multilingual large language models and evaluation. The event is held at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, includes subsidized participation, group bus transfers from Oslo Airport, and provides meals and accommodation options.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: The ProbAI School 2026 is a Probabilistic AI School taking place in Vilnius, Lithuania. It aims to provide an inclusive educational environment covering state‑of‑the‑art machine‑learning and artificial‑intelligence topics for enthusiasts, students, academics and industry professionals. The school is co‑organized with the Artificial Intelligence Association of Lithuania and offers participants hands‑on learning and networking opportunities.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England, UK. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a broad range of computer‑vision topics delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The programme includes daily oral talks, a group photo, and social events such as a dinner and poster reception.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford ML School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: OxML 2026 offers three specialised tracks to upskill in the latest AI theory and applications. Learners can choose any combination of tracks and learn from world‑renowned experts from frontier AI labs in academia and industry. The school is held in Oxford and also available online, continuing the Oxford ML School tradition since 2019.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026 is a six‑day event for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers organized by the Department for Robotics, Perception and Learning at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Sweden. It covers a broad spectrum of topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making, combining keynote talks, industry panels and open brainstorming sessions. Participants benefit from fully funded accommodation, meals and activities at the Happy Tammsvik resort, and the program aims to foster new collaborations and concrete research ideas.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School 2026 is a five‑day event held in Edinburgh that brings together master’s‑level students and industry practitioners to explore robotics. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials and industry talks covering bio‑inspired robotics, healthcare robotics, generative AI, safe AI and real‑world applications, with hands‑on experience using state‑of‑the‑art technology. Participants also benefit from networking opportunities and a special dinner, fostering collaboration across academia and industry.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2026 Biometrics Summer School takes place in Alghero, Sardinia, Italy, hosted at the Hotel Dei Pini. It focuses on the impact of generative AI and large foundation models on biometric and human‑recognition technologies, covering machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, forensic and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers, forensic examiners and professionals, offering intensive lectures by leading experts, hands‑on sessions, and the possibility of scholarships and a short‑paper presentation.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems brings together researchers and students to discuss responsible AI. It offers lectures, multidisciplinary hands‑on training, a poster session and a social program to foster networking and professional exchange. The three‑day event takes place at Umeå University in Sweden from 11 to 13 March 2026.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The ACM Europe Winter School SoRAIM’27 focuses on social robotics, artificial intelligence, and multimedia. It targets PhD students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on sessions, and informal networking in a mountain setting. The program aims to foster cross‑disciplinary exchange among fields such as computer vision, speech processing, affective computing, and human‑robot interaction.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The 2027 Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference includes a Winter School held from 11 to 15 January. It focuses on recent advances in deep learning such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction and speech recognition. The school targets researchers and practitioners who want to exchange ideas, foster collaborations, and learn cutting‑edge techniques.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS) is an 11‑day intensive program offering AI lectures, labs, and project work. It targets senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty, and industry professionals, covering fundamentals to cutting‑edge topics such as Geometric Deep Learning, World Models, Generative Modeling, and Neuro‑symbolic AI. The school brings together over 500 in‑person participants and thousands of online viewers at Kathmandu World School in Kathmandu, Nepal.

name: EEML Summer School
venue: Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School, Cetinje, Montenegro
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. It brings together leading researchers and industry experts to deliver lectures and tutorials on recent advances in machine learning and artificial intelligence. The program targets graduate students and early‑career researchers from the region, offering networking opportunities and exposure to cutting‑edge research.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School is a five‑day program featuring keynotes, lectures, and hands‑on sessions led by international AI experts. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, as well as academics and practitioners, focusing on topics such as computer vision, NLP, generative models, reinforcement learning and ethics. The 2027 edition will be held in Spain in September, offering networking opportunities, poster presentations, and scholarships to promote diversity.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The 2nd edition of the AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI is a five‑day immersive program held at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, Morocco. It offers young researchers, Ph.D. and master’s students, post‑docs, and industry professionals a mix of theoretical lectures, hands‑on labs, and project mentorship on cutting‑edge multimodal and generative AI technologies. The school is jointly organized by MoroccoAI, INPT, IMT Nord Europe and Soft Centre, providing networking opportunities with leading AI experts and fostering the next generation of AI leaders in Morocco.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing Summer School 2026 is a week‑long intensive program on NLP held at the NCSR “Demokritos” campus in Athens, Greece. It is jointly organized by several research institutions and universities, including RC “Athena”, NCSR “Demokritos”, Athens University of Economics and Business, Heriot‑Watt University, Archimedes Unit / Athena RC, and ELLIS – University of Manchester. The school targets students and researchers interested in state‑of‑the‑art NLP techniques and offers lectures, hands‑on sessions, and networking opportunities, while also supporting the adjacent EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning summer school at Lady Margaret Hall focuses on generative AI and deep unsupervised learning techniques. It combines theoretical lectures on clustering, GANs, self‑supervised and energy‑based models with hands‑on projects that apply these methods to real‑world data across various domains. The programme is aimed at STEM students with intermediate AI/ML experience who are considering graduate study or research and offers both residential and online formats.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI brings together researchers, PhD students and post‑doctoral scholars to explore how artificial intelligence can accelerate scientific research. The program covers machine learning for data analysis, AI‑driven experimental design, generative models, and integration of AI with physical simulations, and includes hands‑on workshops using Python libraries such as NumPy and PyTorch. Emphasizing interdisciplinary collaboration, the school aims to equip participants with practical skills to apply deep‑learning techniques to their own scientific problems.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week intensive program held at LUT University’s Lappeenranta campus, offering bachelor’s and master’s level courses in sustainability, climate action, marketing, management and technology. The programme combines lectures, workshops, group work and social activities, allowing participants to gain interdisciplinary knowledge and experience Finnish summer nature. It is aimed at international university students who meet the enrolment criteria and wish to earn 3 ECTS credits while engaging with experts from business and technology fields.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: AIces 2026 is the inaugural International School on the Cognitive, Ethical and Societal Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence, held in Porto and Maia, Portugal. The program targets graduate and postgraduate students as well as industry practitioners, offering parallel courses, live online participation, and face‑to‑face networking. Participants can present in a symposium or open‑debate format and receive a certificate of participation, with all lectures recorded and available for 45 days after the event.
